title: Software Engineer
description: Design, develop, and maintain software applications and systems. Work across web, mobile, or backend infrastructure.
educationPath: BS in CS/IT or coding bootcamp. Strong portfolio often matters more than the degree.
whatYouDo: Write production code 4–6 hours a day
Debug issues and review peers' code
Design system architecture and estimate tasks
Collaborate with product, design, and QA teams

roadmap.action: Job prep — system design + mock interviews

reality.workLife: Variable — intense at startups, calmer at big tech
reality.future: Strong but evolving rapidly with AI

commonMistakes: Learning 5 languages, mastering none
Skipping DSA to 'just build projects'
Not contributing to open source
Chasing FAANG titles without fundamentals
careerChangerPath: Any background → 6-month intensive bootcamp → build 3 real projects → apply to startups → transition in 12–18 months.

title: Data Scientist
description: Extract insights from data using statistics, machine learning, and programming to drive business decisions.
educationPath: BS in Statistics/CS + MS in Data Science, or strong self-taught portfolio.
whatYouDo: Clean and analyze datasets (SQL, Python)
Build and evaluate ML models
Present insights to business teams
Deploy models to production

roadmap.action: Apply to analyst/DS roles, prep case studies

reality.workLife: Balanced at product companies, intense at startups
reality.future: Very strong but evolving — focus shifting to ML engineering

commonMistakes: Doing courses forever, never finishing a project
Ignoring SQL (it's 60% of the job)
Using complex models before understanding data
Not learning to communicate findings to non-tech people

costAndTime.hidden: Cloud credits $100, GPU for deep learning

careerChangerPath: From any analytical role → 6-month Python + SQL + statistics → analyst role → transition to DS over 18–24 months.

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
description: Protect organizations from cyber threats by monitoring networks, identifying vulnerabilities, and responding to incidents.
educationPath: BS in CS/IT + certifications (CEH, CISSP, CompTIA Security+).
whatYouDo: Monitor networks 24/7 for intrusions and anomalies
Run penetration tests and vulnerability scans
Investigate security incidents and write reports
Patch systems and educate teams on security

roadmap.action: Specialize — pentesting, cloud security, or forensics

reality.workLife: Variable — SOC roles have shifts, consulting is intense
reality.future: Very strong — cyberattacks rising every year

commonMistakes: Learning tools without understanding networking basics
Skipping Linux — 80% of security work is on Linux
Not practicing hands-on (TryHackMe/HackTheBox)
Chasing certifications without real projects
careerChangerPath: Any IT background → 6 months of TryHackMe + Security+ → junior SOC analyst → specialize in pentesting or cloud security within 2 years.

title: UX/UI Designer
description: Craft intuitive and beautiful digital experiences by researching user needs and designing interfaces.
educationPath: B.Des, or any degree + UX bootcamp + strong portfolio.
whatYouDo: Interview users to understand pain points
Sketch wireframes and build Figma prototypes
Run usability tests and iterate on feedback
Collaborate with developers to ship features

roadmap.action: Learn design fundamentals — color, type, layout
roadmap.resource: Refactoring UI, Design of Everyday Things

roadmap.action: Build portfolio of 5 case studies (with process, not just pretty screens)
Apply to 20+ junior roles + design internships
Specialize — product, UX research, or design systems

reality.workLife: Balanced — regular hours at product companies
reality.stress: Medium — iteration cycles can be long
reality.future: Strong — every product needs good UX

commonMistakes: Showing final screens without the design process
Learning tools without learning principles
Copying Dribbble shots without real problems
Ignoring accessibility (WCAG, contrast, keyboard nav)

costAndTime.time: 3 years degree or 6–12 month bootcamp + portfolio

careerChangerPath: Any background → 6-month self-study → 3 strong case studies → freelance/small-agency start → product company in 12–18 months.

title: Doctor (Physician)
description: Diagnose and treat illnesses, improve patient health, and save lives across specialties like cardiology, pediatrics, and surgery.
educationPath: BS + MD (4 yrs) + Residency (3–7 yrs). Total 11+ years after high school.
whatYouDo: Examine 20–50 patients daily (depending on specialty)
Diagnose conditions from symptoms and tests
Prescribe treatments and follow up on progress
Attend emergencies and night shifts

roadmap.action: Choose specialty — internal medicine, surgery, etc.
Build patient base, consider hospital vs. private practice

reality.workLife: Demanding — long hours, night shifts, high stakes
reality.future: Always in demand, aging population ensures stability

commonMistakes: Choosing medicine for prestige, not calling
Ignoring mental health during MCAT prep
Not researching specialties before residency choice
Underestimating the financial cost of medical school

costAndTime.hidden: MCAT prep, books, relocation, exam fees

careerChangerPath: Not typical — requires full pre-med + MD restart. Alternative: healthcare management, medical writing, pharma.

title: Registered Nurse
description: Provide direct patient care, administer medications, and support doctors in hospitals and clinics.
educationPath: BSN (4 yrs) or ADN (2 yrs) + NCLEX-RN licensure.

title: Physiotherapist
description: Help patients recover from injuries and improve mobility through exercise, massage, and manual therapy.
educationPath: DPT (Doctor of Physical Therapy, 3 yrs after bachelor's) + licensure.

title: Clinical Psychologist
description: Diagnose and treat mental health conditions through therapy and counseling sessions.
educationPath: BA/BS Psychology → PhD/PsyD → state licensure.

title: Chartered Accountant
description: Manage financial audits, taxation, and business advisory for companies and individuals.
educationPath: BS in Accounting + CPA exam (4 sections) + state license.
whatYouDo: Audit company financials for accuracy
Prepare tax returns and compliance reports
Advise clients on business structuring
Represent clients before tax authorities

roadmap.action: BS Accounting — 150 credit hours for CPA

reality.workLife: Intense during tax season, flexible otherwise

commonMistakes: Underestimating CPA exam difficulty
Neglecting practical experience (internships matter)
Not building IT and communication skills
Giving up after one failed exam section

costAndTime.hidden: 150 credit hours requirement often means extra semester

careerChangerPath: Any bachelor's + accounting credits → CPA exam → entry-level accounting role. Expect 2–3 years part-time.

title: Investment Banker
description: Help companies raise capital, execute mergers & acquisitions, and manage financial strategy.
educationPath: BS in Finance/Econ + MBA (Finance) from top-tier program.

title: Marketing Manager
description: Plan and execute campaigns to promote products, build brand awareness, and drive customer acquisition.
educationPath: BS in Marketing/Business + MBA (Marketing) for senior roles.
whatYouDo: Plan campaigns across digital and traditional channels
Analyze customer data to find what works
Manage a team of writers, designers, and analysts
Report ROI to leadership and adjust strategy

roadmap.action: Build a blog or social media presence
Study marketing or business + run side projects
Start as marketing associate or coordinator

reality.remote: Very good — most roles are hybrid or remote
reality.future: Strong — every company needs marketing, but AI is shifting tactics

commonMistakes: Focusing on creativity without data — modern marketing is 50% analytics
Not learning SEO and paid ads basics
Ignoring storytelling and copywriting skills
Underestimating the value of a portfolio of campaigns

costAndTime.time: 4-year degree + 2–3 years of experience to reach manager

careerChangerPath: Any background → 6-month marketing certificate + freelance projects → junior marketing role → manager in 3–4 years.

title: HR Manager
description: Recruit talent, manage employee relations, and shape company culture and policies.
educationPath: BS in HR/Business + MBA or SHRM-CP certification.

title: Graphic Designer
description: Create visual content for branding, advertising, digital media, and print using design tools.
educationPath: BFA/B.Des, or self-taught + strong portfolio. Freelancing common.
whatYouDo: Create visuals for brands, ads, social media
Collaborate with copywriters and marketing teams
Iterate on designs based on client feedback
Prepare files for print/digital production

roadmap.action: Redesign real brands as case studies
Niche down — branding, packaging, or UI

reality.workLife: Variable — freelance is feast or famine
reality.stress: Medium — client revisions can be draining
reality.future: Evolving — AI tools change the workflow

commonMistakes: Underpricing early work
Taking every client regardless of fit
Not learning business/contract skills
Only knowing one tool (learn Adobe + Figma + Canva)

costAndTime.time: 6 months to a year to reach $2K/mo freelance

careerChangerPath: Learn Figma + Canva in 3 months → offer free work to 3 small businesses → build case studies → start charging → scale.

title: Content Writer
description: Write blogs, articles, scripts, and marketing copy for brands and publications.
educationPath: Any degree + writing portfolio. Journalism/English helps.

title: Film Director
description: Lead the creative vision of films, web series, and video content — from script to screen.
educationPath: Film school (NYU, USC, AFI) or hands-on experience + portfolio.

title: Architect
description: Design buildings and spaces balancing aesthetics, functionality, and safety.
educationPath: B.Arch (5 yrs) + state licensure (NCARB).

title: Civil Engineer
description: Design, build, and maintain infrastructure — bridges, roads, dams, and buildings.
educationPath: BS Civil Engineering + PE license for senior roles.
whatYouDo: Design structures and infrastructure with AutoCAD
Analyze loads, stresses, and safety requirements
Coordinate with contractors and city officials
Visit sites to inspect construction progress

roadmap.action: Work 4 years under a PE (Professional Engineer)

reality.workLife: Moderate — some travel to sites, otherwise office
reality.remote: Partial — site visits need in-person, design is remote
reality.future: Strong — infrastructure investment keeps growing globally

commonMistakes: Skipping internships — practical experience is essential
Not pursuing PE license — costs you 30% higher salary ceiling
Ignoring software skills (AutoCAD, Revit, Civil 3D)
Choosing a specialty too early (explore structural, transportation, environmental)

costAndTime.hidden: FE + PE exam fees $700 total, software $200/yr

careerChangerPath: Engineering technician → BS Civil Engineering (part-time possible) → FE exam → junior engineer → PE license in 8 years total.

title: Mechanical Engineer
description: Design and manufacture machines, engines, and mechanical systems across industries.
educationPath: BS Mechanical Engineering + PE license optional.

title: Electrical Engineer
description: Design and maintain electrical systems for power, electronics, and automation.
educationPath: BS Electrical Engineering + PE license for senior roles.

title: School Teacher
description: Educate and inspire students, shape young minds, and foster a love for learning.
educationPath: Bachelor's in subject + teaching certification (state-specific).
whatYouDo: Plan lessons and teach 5–6 classes daily
Grade assignments, exams, and give feedback
Mentor students and communicate with parents
Attend staff meetings and professional development

roadmap.action: Bachelor's in your subject + teacher prep program
Get classroom experience + pursue master's for higher pay

reality.future: Stable demand — always need teachers, though pay varies wildly by state

commonMistakes: Choosing teaching for summers off — the job is harder than it looks
Not researching salary by state — varies from $40K to $90K+
Skipping classroom management training
Ignoring mental health — teacher burnout is real

costAndTime.hidden: Certification exams $300, student teaching is unpaid

careerChangerPath: Any bachelor's degree → alternative certification program (1 year) → classroom teaching. Common for career-changers in STEM fields.

title: University Professor
description: Teach at universities, conduct research, and mentor the next generation of scholars.
educationPath: Master's → PhD → postdoc or tenure-track position.

title: Government Administrator
description: Administer public policy, lead government departments, and serve communities at senior levels.
educationPath: Any bachelor's degree + civil service exam (varies by country).

title: Military Officer
description: Serve in the armed forces — lead troops, defend borders, and build discipline and strategy.
educationPath: Military academy (ROTC, West Point, etc.) or officer candidate school.

title: Entrepreneur
description: Build your own company, solve problems, and create value — from startup idea to scaled business.
educationPath: No formal requirement — business degree or MBA helpful.
whatYouDo: Talk to customers — every single day
Build and iterate on your product
Manage cash flow, hiring, and team culture
Pitch to investors and partners

roadmap.action: Read startup fundamentals, follow founders on X
Solve a real problem you have
Iterate fast, track metrics, hire slowly
Find product-market fit or pivot within 12 months

reality.stress: Extremely high — you own every problem

commonMistakes: Building without talking to customers first
Chasing investors before having a product
Hiring too fast, firing too slow
Running out of cash because you didn't watch runway

costAndTime.hidden: Opportunity cost — you're not earning a salary

careerChangerPath: Start while employed. Build a side project → earn first $100 → quit when it covers 6 months of expenses.
